sections.h2: How does selling a house in Cuyahoga Falls work?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell it yourself, or take a cash offer from a buyer who purchases the house as it stands. All three routes finish in the same place in Summit County: both sides sign the city's stormwater disclosure, a deed is prepared, and the county Fiscal Office transfers and records it. What changes from route to route is the wait, who pays for repairs, and how much risk the seller carries.

Cuyahoga Falls lies directly north of Akron and is the second-largest city in Summit County. The Census Bureau lists 25.80 square miles of land, a 2020 count of 51,114 people and a July 2025 estimate of 50,975. That is a drop of 0.2 percent from the 2020 estimates base, so the city is steady rather than booming.

sections.h2: What in the city's past shapes the houses a seller is dealing with?
sections.html:
A river power town became a residential suburb, and that history explains both the street pattern and the school boundaries. Settlers dammed the Cuyahoga River in 1812 to run mills, and the community was first called Manchester before the Post Office pushed a rename. By the middle of the twentieth century the mills had faded and the city was mostly homes.

The census tallies show how quickly that happened: 20,546 residents in 1940 and 47,922 in 1960. If your house was built in those decades, expect buyers to ask about sewer laterals, gutters and downspouts, which is exactly what the city's stormwater inspection covers.

In 1986 the city merged with Northampton Township, the first merger of a city and a township in Ohio. The former township territory sits in the northwest and still has its own school district, which matters when you describe the property to buyers.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about homes in Cuyahoga Falls?
sections.html:
The numbers describe a mid-priced Summit County suburb where most households own. These figures come from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts table for 2020 through 2024 unless noted.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $183,300.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 64.4 percent, across 23,212 households.
  • Median gross rent: $1,038 a month; median owner cost with a mortgage: $1,349.
  • Median household income: $72,705, with a mean commute of 21.6 minutes.
  • 2020 Census housing count: 24,827 units, of which 5.7 percent were vacant, with a 1.1 percent homeowner vacancy rate.

A 1.1 percent homeowner vacancy rate means few owner-occupied homes sit empty, so a house that needs work is competing with move-in ready listings for the same buyers.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve houses in Cuyahoga Falls?
sections.html:
Most of the city is in the Cuyahoga Falls City School District, but four districts touch the city limits. The original city area makes up nearly all of that district, and Cuyahoga Falls High School stands near downtown. The village of Silver Lake belongs to it too.

The former Northampton Township area is served by Woodridge Local School District, whose high school is in Cuyahoga Falls even though its mailing address says Peninsula. A small slice of the northeast is zoned to Hudson City School District, and a sliver of the far northwest is in Revere Local School District. Confirm the district for your parcel before you put a district name in a listing.

sections.h2: What does the stormwater inspection mean for a Cuyahoga Falls sale?
sections.html:
The city runs a free stormwater inspection, and it asks that the buyer and the seller of any house sign the related disclosure. The inspection looks for clean water getting into the sanitary sewer from private property, such as downspouts or footer drains tied to the wrong pipe. Anything that violates city code must be repaired within 180 days after the inspection.

Chapter 1306 of the city's codified ordinances sets the mechanics:

  • The owner, or a buyer under contract, may ask the city to inspect sewer laterals, sewer connections, gutters, downspouts and footer drains.
  • The city does the work at its own cost and may use a sewer camera, smoke or dye testing.
  • A Certificate of Inspection goes to the owner, and to the buyer if the buyer asked, within ten days.
  • An owner who holds a certificate must hand a copy to the purchaser before transferring the property.
  • After repairs, the owner can request a Certificate of Completion.

The chapter also says no one may sell sewer-served property without telling the buyer that the inspection is available, using a city form. A violation is a misdemeanor of the fourth degree. The request form sits in the housing and development section of the city's permits and forms page.

sections.h2: What happens if my house has code problems?
sections.html:
The city's housing division enforces property maintenance and zoning rules through inspections and complaint investigations. Complaints can be made anonymously, and each one is tracked. The development department takes calls at (330) 971-8135.

The city lists these as its most common violations: overgrown weeds, trees or shrubs; trash and refuse; abandoned or inoperable vehicles, boats and trailers; structures such as garages, sheds and fences that are not sound; and animal waste left on a lawn. Clearing a yard or hauling off a derelict trailer costs far less than negotiating around it at a buyer's inspection. If you inherited the house and have not been inside in months, check the yard first.

sections.h2: What must a seller hand the buyer under Ohio law?
sections.html:
For a house or a building with up to four dwelling units, Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 requires the owner to complete the state property disclosure form and give a signed copy to the buyer as soon as practicable. A buyer who receives the form after making an offer can rescind in writing within three business days of receiving it, as long as that happens by the earlier of thirty days after acceptance or closing.

Several transfers are exempt. One that matters in Summit County estate sales is a transfer by someone who inherited the property and did not live there during the previous year. Court-ordered transfers and transfers by an estate's fiduciary are also listed as exempt.

sections.h2: What do deed transfer and recording cost in Summit County?
sections.html:
Summit County charges a conveyance fee at transfer plus a recording fee at the recorder's counter. The Fiscal Office posts these charges on its fee page and its recording FAQ.

Summit County Fiscal Office charges for a sale (source: Fiscal Office fee page and recording FAQ)
ItemRate as posted
Conveyance fee$4.00 per $1000, rounded up to the next $100 of the sale price
Lot fee50 cents per lot in the legal description
Recording a deed$34 for two pages, $8 per added page
Copy of a recorded deed$4, plus $1 if certified
Recording turnaround3 to 5 working days

The Fiscal Office says the recording division does not run title or property searches, so your title company handles that. To change names on a deed, a new deed must be prepared, and Ohio law lets only the person asking for the change or an attorney prepare it. The office has temporarily relocated during building construction, so check its website for the service location before you go in person.

sections.h2: When does a cash offer suit a Cuyahoga Falls seller?
sections.html:
A cash offer suits sellers who want certainty about the closing date and prefer not to fix sewer or code items first. Houses with open stormwater items, deferred maintenance, tenants, or an inherited title that needs sorting are the usual cases. A buyer who purchases as-is takes on those items, and you can usually choose a closing date that fits your move.

Weigh any offer against what listing would net after repairs, the carrying cost of waiting, and the 180-day repair clock that follows a failed stormwater inspection. Ask each buyer to put the price, the closing date and who pays closing costs in writing, and compare them side by side.

faqs.q: Do I need a stormwater inspection to sell in Cuyahoga Falls?
faqs.a: The signed disclosure is required for a sale, and the inspection itself is free on request. Under Chapter 1306, either the owner or a buyer under contract can ask the city to inspect, and any owner who has a Certificate of Inspection must give the buyer a copy.

faqs.q: How soon must stormwater problems be fixed?
faqs.a: Within 180 days after an inspection, according to the city's stormwater inspection page. After repairs, the owner can ask the city for a Certificate of Completion stating the listed violations were corrected.

faqs.q: How long does Summit County take to record a deed?
faqs.a: The Fiscal Office gives a turnaround of 3 to 5 working days. The recording division's phone number on its FAQ page is 330-643-2712, and e-recording through approved vendors is available.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Cuyahoga Falls house in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in Cuyahoga Falls City Schools, the former Northampton Township area is in Woodridge Local, and small parts are in Hudson City or Revere Local. Check your parcel with the county before you advertise a district.

faqs.q: Can the buyer back out after reading the Ohio disclosure form?
faqs.a: Only in limited cases. If the form arrives after the buyer made an offer, the buyer may rescind in writing within three business days of receiving it, and no later than the earlier of thirty days after acceptance or closing.
